OVF Server Explorer -- install instructions (KNIME 4.1.x)
=========================================================

Adds a Server Explorer view to KNIME that browses a remote HTTP
workflow share or a local filesystem mount. This is NOT an official
KNIME product; it is a third-party plugin under the org.ovf.* namespace.

This build targets KNIME 4.1.x (Java 8 runtime, Eclipse 4.7 workbench).
For KNIME 5.x use the 5.x zip instead.


A guide with pictures: INSTALL-GUIDE.html in the installer zip, or
https://shinwachi.github.io/ovf-updates/install.html


-----------------------------------------------------------------
Step 1: choose who gets the plugin
-----------------------------------------------------------------

  All users (admin)   Installs into the KNIME folder. Everyone using this
                      KNIME gets it. Use this when people share one KNIME.
                      You need administrator rights.

  Just me (user)      Installs into your own home folder. Nobody else sees
                      it. You need no special rights. Each person has to
                      repeat it, and each gets their own copy to update.
                      If an administrator later changes this KNIME, the plugin
                      stops loading until you finish KNIME's Migration wizard
                      or run the installer again.

If you are not sure and you have administrator rights, choose All users.


-----------------------------------------------------------------
Step 2: run the installer
-----------------------------------------------------------------

Quit KNIME, extract the installer zip

    ovf-serverconnector-4.1.x-@VERSION@-installer.zip

to any folder, then:

  Windows   All users: right-click install-ovf.cmd > Run as administrator
            Just me:   double-click install-ovf.cmd

  Linux     All users: sudo ./install-ovf.sh
            Just me:   ./install-ovf.sh

It offers to scan this computer for KNIME and list what it finds, or to let you
select knime.exe (Windows) or knime (Linux) in a file picker. You can also type
the folder. Run it once for each KNIME that should have the plugin.
Then it asks who gets the plugin, checks the folder's
permissions, installs, then lists where the files are. To only see the report,
changing nothing:

    install-ovf.cmd -Knime "C:\Program Files\KNIME" -Check
    ./install-ovf.sh --knime /opt/knime --check

Restart KNIME. The Server Explorer tab appears next to KNIME Explorer.


-----------------------------------------------------------------
Where the files are, and who should have access
-----------------------------------------------------------------

To find the KNIME folder: it holds knime.exe (Windows) or knime (Linux), and
knime.ini, plugins and configuration. On Windows, right-click the KNIME
shortcut > Open file location. Common places:

    C:\Program Files\KNIME        /opt/knime

  What              Where                                  Who needs access
  ----------------  -------------------------------------  --------------------
  KNIME folder      as above                               Admins: full control
  (program files;                                          Everyone else: read
  all-users plugin                                         and execute only, on
  in plugins)                                              all files inside

  Private area      Windows: C:\Users\<you>\.eclipse\<id>  Only that person.
  (just-for-me      Linux:   ~/.eclipse/<id>               KNIME creates it.
  plugin in                                                Don't change or share
  plugins; one                                             it.
  per person)

  Workspace         KNIME asks at startup. By default:     Only that person.
  (layout and       Windows: C:\Users\<you>\knime-workspace  Two people must not
  settings in       Linux:   ~/knime-workspace             open one workspace
  .metadata)                                               at once.

<id> is a number followed by the platform, such as 1877637008_linux_gtk_x86_64.
If you can't see .eclipse, paste the path into File Explorer's address bar.

To set the KNIME folder permissions as recommended, as an administrator:

  Windows (Command Prompt; or add -ApplyPermissions to the installer):

    icacls "C:\Program Files\KNIME" /reset /T /C /Q
    icacls "C:\Program Files\KNIME" /inheritance:r /grant:r *S-1-5-32-544:(OI)(CI)F *S-1-5-18:(OI)(CI)F *S-1-5-32-545:(OI)(CI)RX

    Check it under right-click the folder > Properties > Security.

  Linux (or add --apply-permissions to the installer):

    sudo chown -R root:root /opt/knime
    sudo chmod -R go-w,a+rX /opt/knime

Permissions that cause trouble on the KNIME folder:

  Users can create files but not change them
      KNIME can't lock its own files: installs fail or do nothing, and nodes go
      missing from the Node Repository. The installer reports this and stops.
      On Windows this is the default if KNIME is unzipped outside Program Files,
      for example into a folder under C:\. Use the commands above to fix it.

  Users can change everything (Everyone: Full control)
      One user can uninstall the plugin for everybody. And if the files one
      user creates can't be changed by the next, the next user's KNIME may not
      start. The usual error is "See the log file null".


-----------------------------------------------------------------
Other ways to install
-----------------------------------------------------------------

KNIME's own wizard (File > Install KNIME Extensions..., Add..., Archive...,
pick ovf-serverconnector-4.1.x-@VERSION@-updatesite.zip). It can't ask who the
plugin is for: if you can't write to the KNIME folder it installs for you only;
if you can, it installs for everyone. KNIME warns that the plugin is unsigned:
choose Install anyway. A live site also works:
https://shinwachi.github.io/ovf-updates/4.1.x/

Dropin, for all users (administrator): quit KNIME, extract
ovf-serverconnector-4.1.x-@VERSION@.zip so that this file exists, and start KNIME
once with -clean:

    <KNIME folder>/dropins/serverconnector/plugins/org.ovf.serverconnector_@BUNDLE_VERSION@.jar


Workspaces need no change, for either kind of install. The plugin adds its tab
when a workspace opens. Each workspace keeps its own list of servers.


-----------------------------------------------------------------
If something looks wrong
-----------------------------------------------------------------

No Server Explorer tab
    Check you are in the same account the plugin was installed for, and that
    you restarted KNIME. If you closed the tab earlier, it stays closed:
    View > Other... > KNIME Views > Server Explorer > Open

Red Server Explorer tab and a Migration wizard
    Your just-for-me copy stopped loading because an administrator changed this
    KNIME. Finish the wizard, or cancel it and run the installer again.

"knime.ini sets KNIME's configuration" when installing for all users
    An all-users install would damage that setting and KNIME wouldn't start.
    Take the -configuration lines out of knime.ini, install, then put them back.
    A just-for-me install handles the setting by itself.

Which install do I have?
    File > Preferences > Server Connector says who has it, and where the files
    are.

"Server Explorer (needs OVF plugin)" with a red mark, or "Could not create the
view: org.ovf.serverconnector.views.ServerExplorerView"
    This workspace was used with the plugin, and this KNIME doesn't have it.
    Nothing is lost. Install the plugin, or close that tab. The tab returns
    next time you use this workspace in a KNIME that has the plugin.

KNIME won't start, or the Node Repository is short of nodes
    The KNIME folder's permissions are the likely cause. Run the installer's
    check, above.


-----------------------------------------------------------------
Configure
-----------------------------------------------------------------

File > Preferences > Server Connector > Servers


-----------------------------------------------------------------
Uninstall
-----------------------------------------------------------------

Run the installer the same way you installed, with one more option:

    install-ovf.cmd -Knime "<KNIME folder>" -Mode admin -Uninstall   (or user)
    ./install-ovf.sh --knime <KNIME folder> --mode admin --uninstall  (or user)

If you used the wizard: Help > About KNIME > Installation Details > select
"OVF Server Explorer" > Uninstall...

If you used the dropin: quit KNIME, delete <KNIME folder>/dropins/serverconnector,
and start KNIME once with -clean.
